name: Mind training (blo sbyong)
method_summary: Training the mind in relative and ultimate bodhicitta by means of short slogans applied throughout the day: after the preliminaries, meditating on phenomena as dream-like and resting in the mind's nature (ultimate), practising sending and taking on the breath (relative), turning every adversity into the path, applying the five powers in life and at death, checking one's progress, and keeping the commitments and precepts.
prerequisites: the four thoughts that turn the mind
signs_of_progress: one can practise even when distracted (Seven Points 5.4)
one's own mind as the principal witness (5.2)

warnings.text: Do not let the gods descend into demons — mind training that increases pride is inverted.
Abandon poisoned food — virtue mixed with self-grasping.
Do not act with a twist — practising mind training for selfish ends.

equivalents.note: lojong includes and systematises Śāntideva's exchange

name: Sending and taking (gtong len)
method_summary: Visualising the suffering of others (beginning with one's own future suffering) and its causes, one takes it in on the in-breath, dissolving it into one's own self-cherishing; on the out-breath one sends one's body, happiness and virtue to them, imagining them satisfied; applied to the three objects and three poisons, and used when suffering or witnessing suffering.
stage: intermediate (after love and compassion are developed)

warnings.text: Begin the sequence of taking with yourself.
Do the taking secretly, without display (Eight Verses 7: 'secretly take upon myself').

equivalents.note: tonglen is the meditative technique of the exchange

name: Meditation on the stages of the path
method_summary: Daily sessions in which, after the six preparatory practices, one takes one lamrim topic (the teacher, leisure and endowment, death, the lower realms, refuge, karma, saṃsāra's faults, the twelve links, bodhicitta, the perfections, calm, insight) as the subject of analytical meditation until a felt conviction arises, then holds it with placement meditation; ends with dedication; the whole cycle is repeated.

name: Analytical meditation (dpyad sgom)
method_summary: Meditation that repeatedly investigates the object with discernment and reasoning — e.g. the reasons for the certainty of death, the kindness of beings, the one-or-many analysis of the self — to produce and strengthen conviction; alternated with placement meditation on the conclusion reached.

warnings.text: If analysis is overdone before calm is stable, stability declines; if placement alone is done on topics needing conviction, no transformation occurs — both are needed in balance.

equivalents.note: the special case with emptiness as object

name: Placement meditation ('jog sgom)
method_summary: Holding the mind one-pointedly on its object without analysis — the method for calm abiding and for stabilising a conclusion reached by analysis.

name: Calm abiding according to the lamrim
method_summary: Having gathered the prerequisites, one sits in the eight-featured posture, takes an object (often the visualised body of the Buddha), and progresses through the nine mental states by the six powers and four attentions, applying the eight antidotes to the five faults — above all recognising gross and subtle laxity and excitement with alertness — until pliancy of mind and body arises.
prerequisites: the six prerequisites (suitable place, few desires, contentment, few activities, pure ethics, abandoning desire-thoughts)
duration: months to years of continuous practice (the texts give no fixed measure)
signs_of_progress: the nine mental states in order
mental then physical pliancy with joy
the mind stays on its object at will

warnings.text: Subtle laxity is easily mistaken for faultless meditation; long meditation in it dulls the mind.
If the limbs of calm are lost, even thousands of years of effort will not produce concentration.

equivalents.note: same ninefold method from the Śrāvakabhūmi
Kamalaśīla's presentation, on which the lamrim draws

name: The seven-point cause-and-effect meditation for bodhicitta
method_summary: Establishing equanimity toward friends, enemies and strangers, then meditating in sequence: all beings have been one's mother; their kindness as mothers; the wish to repay it; affectionate love; great compassion; the extraordinary resolve to free them oneself; and bodhicitta.

equivalents.note: the other lamrim method for bodhicitta; Gelug teachers often combine the two

name: Taking adversity as the path
method_summary: When harmed or in bad circumstances, blaming self-cherishing rather than others, contemplating the harmer's kindness as a teacher of patience, seeing the situation as empty and like a dream, and doing the four practices — so that illness, enemies and loss become aids to bodhicitta.

name: The four practices (sbyor ba bzhi)
method_summary: Accumulating merit, purifying wrongdoing, offering torma to harmful spirits (thanking them for the chance to train), and offering to the dharma protectors — used to take adverse circumstances onto the path.

name: Mind-training transference at death (the five powers)
method_summary: At death one gives away one's possessions (white seed), confesses and purifies, and applies the five powers — resolve, familiarity, white seed, repudiation, aspiration — lying in the lion posture and practising sending and taking, then resting in the nature of mind.

name: Contemplating the four thoughts that turn the mind
method_summary: Repeated analytical contemplation of the precious human life, death and impermanence, karma and its results, and the sufferings of saṃsāra until the mind turns from this life and from saṃsāra.

name: The six preparatory practices of a lamrim session
method_summary: Cleaning the room and setting up representations of body, speech and mind; arranging offerings; sitting in the proper posture and taking refuge and generating bodhicitta; visualising the field of merit; offering the seven limbs and the maṇḍala; making requests to the lineage.

name: Atiśa's daily conduct of a bodhisattva
method_summary: Rising in the last part of the night and recollecting the nature of phenomena; seeing appearances as illusion; seven-limb practice and aspiration; eating moderately with the body regarded as a boat and food divided in four offerings; circumambulation and recitation; the ten dharma practices with mindfulness; resting the mind free of elaboration in the first part of the night; sleeping in the lion posture with the notion of light.

name: Examining the mind day and night (Kadam self-watching)
method_summary: Checking one's mind-stream three times by day and three by night, proclaiming one's own faults, watching speech in company and mind when alone; the Kadam hermit Ben Gungyal counted his virtuous and non-virtuous thoughts with white and black pebbles.
notes: The pebble anecdote of Ben Gungyal is recalled from lojong and lamrim literature, not tied here to a verse.

name: The sixteen drops of the Kadam (bka' gdams thig le bcu drug)
method_summary: A guru-yoga visualisation of nested drops containing the lineage teachers, Kadam deities and the practitioner, taught in the Book of Kadam as the Kadam heart practice.
notes: Recalled only in outline; details not recorded.

name: Sleeping in the lion posture
method_summary: Lying on the right side like a lion (as the Buddha at his passing), with the notion of rising and of light, falling asleep in virtue.

name: Recitation of the Migtsema
method_summary: Repeating the Migtsema praise of Tsongkhapa as a mantra, often within the Hundred Deities of Tuṣita guru yoga, with visualisations of nectar and light for purification and for gaining wisdom.

name: Gelug Mahāmudrā meditation on the mind
method_summary: After preliminaries and guru yoga, one takes the mind itself — its mere clarity and knowing — as the object of calm abiding; then, with that calm, investigates the mind's way of existing to realise its emptiness; alternately in the mantra approach through the clear light.

equivalents.note: the Kagyu Mahāmudrā practice; the Gelug root text says both converge in one intent

name: Lamdre contemplation of the three visions
method_summary: Contemplating in order the impure vision (sufferings of saṃsāra, the difficulty of leisure and endowment, death, karma), the experiential vision (love, compassion, relative and ultimate bodhicitta, and the experiences of meditation) and the pure vision (the qualities of buddhahood) as the preliminary of the Lamdre.

name: Contemplation of Parting from the Four Attachments
method_summary: Taking each line in turn as a meditation: the uselessness of practice for this life, the faults of saṃsāra, the need for bodhicitta, and resting in the view free of grasping at extremes.

name: Hevajra practice in the Sakya
method_summary: After receiving the Hevajra empowerment of the Lamdre, the practitioner daily performs the Hevajra sādhana of the generation stage and, under instruction, the completion-stage practices of the method continuum; the daily practice is a commitment of those empowered.
prerequisites: the Lamdre Tsokshé or Lobshé instruction

warnings.text: Completion-stage practices of the body-method continuum are restricted; the Vajra Verses list obstacles and their protections.

notes: Summary only; restricted completion-stage content not recorded.

name: Exchanging self and other
method_summary: In the lamrim and lojong: after equalizing, contemplating the faults of self-cherishing and the benefits of cherishing others, then exchanging the objects of cherishing, enacted by sending and taking.

name: Equalizing self and other
method_summary: Reflecting that oneself and all others equally want happiness and do not want suffering, so there is no ground for cherishing oneself above them; the first step of Śāntideva's method as taught in the lamrim.

name: The nine mental abidings
method_summary: As taught in the Lamrim Chenmo: the nine states achieved by six powers and four attentions, abandoning five faults with eight antidotes.

name: The eight antidotes to the five faults
method_summary: Faith, aspiration, effort and pliancy against laziness; mindfulness against forgetting the instruction; alertness to notice laxity and excitement; application of the remedy against non-application; equanimity against over-application.

name: Analytical meditation on emptiness
method_summary: In the Gelug: identifying the object of negation as it appears to innate self-grasping, then applying the sevenfold or four-point analysis until its absence is ascertained, and alternating this with placement on that absence; Atiśa: ascertaining by scripture and reasoning that phenomena are unborn, then meditating non-conceptually.

name: Going for refuge
method_summary: Atiśa: after offerings and the seven limbs, kneeling with joined palms, going for refuge three times with irreversible intent; Gelug: refuge from fear and faith, with its precepts.

name: The seven-limb practice
method_summary: The sevenfold worship of the Samantabhadra prayer (prostration, offering, confession, rejoicing, requesting teaching, requesting the teachers to remain, dedication), done before refuge (Atiśa) and in every lamrim session.

name: Taking the bodhisattva vow
method_summary: Atiśa: taken from a qualified teacher by the rite of the Bodhisattvabhūmi's ethics chapter, or, lacking a teacher, by Mañjuśrī's (Ambarāja's) rite before the buddhas; requires a prātimokṣa basis.

name: Generating bodhicitta
method_summary: Preceded by love, contemplating beings' sufferings and resolving irreversibly to free them; then taking the aspiring mind by ritual and repeating it.

name: Purification by the four opponent powers
method_summary: Confessing wrongdoing with regret, relying on refuge and bodhicitta, applying a remedy (recitation, prostration, meditation on emptiness) and resolving not to repeat it.

name: Contemplating death
method_summary: The lamrim's meditation on death by three roots, nine reasons and three decisions.

name: Relying on the spiritual teacher
method_summary: Relying in thought — seeing the teacher's qualities and remembering his kindness — and in deed — offering, service and practising as taught; the teacher first examined for the ten qualities.

name: Guru yoga
method_summary: Visualising the teacher as inseparable from the Buddha — Tsongkhapa with his two sons in the Hundred Deities of Tuṣita, or Lobsang Thubwang Dorje Chang in the Offering to the Spiritual Master — offering the seven limbs and maṇḍala, making requests, receiving blessings and dissolving the teacher into oneself.

name: Deity yoga
method_summary: Generating oneself as the deity from emptiness, maintaining divine pride and clear appearance; for the Gelug, the wisdom realising emptiness itself appears as the deity.

name: Monastic debate as practice
method_summary: In the Gelug curriculum debate extends beyond epistemology to all five great texts; the challenger's clap and the defender's formal answers train precise analysis, and debate is regarded as a form of analytical meditation.

name: The ten dharma practices
method_summary: Atiśa's advice to practise day and night the ten dharma practices taught by Maitreya (copying, offering, giving, listening, reading, memorising, explaining, reciting, reflecting, meditating).

name: Guarding the mind with mindfulness and alertness
method_summary: Guarding the doors of the senses with mindfulness, alertness and conscientiousness; examining the mind-stream three times each day and night.

name: Practice with an action-seal (consort)
method_summary: Summary only: completion-stage yoga with a consort, belonging to the higher empowerments. The Kadam and Gelug traditions restrict it: celibate monastics may not take the secret and wisdom empowerments literally, and Gelug monks practise with a visualised consort.

warnings.text: The secret and wisdom empowerments must not be taken by celibates; one who does breaks the vow of austerity, incurs defeat, falls to the lower realms and gains no accomplishment.

name: Inner heat (gtum mo)
method_summary: Summary only: the completion-stage practice of kindling inner heat at the navel, which Tsongkhapa calls the foundation stone of the completion stage; taught in the Six Yogas and within the Lamdre's method continuum.

warnings.text: To be practised only after the common path, a complete empowerment and the generation stage, under a teacher; wind practices done wrongly cause wind disorders.
